questions.q: In ten observations, the mean of all& $10$ numbers is $15$, the mean of the first six observations is $16$ and the mean of the last five observations is $12$. The sixth number is
questions.solution:
Let the mean of the last four observations be ${A}_{2}$. Then, by the formula for combined mean, we get,

$15 = \dfrac{6 \times 16 + 4 \times {A}_{2}}{6 + 4}$~

or $150 = 96 + 4{A}_{2}$~

$∴ {A}_{2} = \dfrac{54}{4}$

Let the sixth number is~$x$, then taking the sixth number as a collection, the combined mean of this collection and the collection of the last four is $12$.

$∴$ By the definition of combined mean

$12 = \dfrac{1 \times x + 4 \times \dfrac{54}{4}}{1 + 4}$

$∴ 60 = x + 54 ∴ x = 6$

Hence, the sixth number $= 6$

questions.q: If mean deviation about the mean of the numbers& $2\lambda, 4\lambda, 6\lambda, 8\lambda, . . . . . , 200\lambda$~is~$100$, the median of the given numbers can be
questions.solution:
Given data is& $2\lambda, 4\lambda, 6\lambda, 8\lambda, . . . . . , 200\lambda$

Mean,~$\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{2\lambda + 4\lambda + 6\lambda + . . . . . + 200\lambda}{100} = \dfrac{2\lambda \cdot \dfrac{100}{2}\left[1 + 100\right]}{100}$

$\overset{¯}{x} = 101\lambda$

Given, mean deviation about mean is~$100$

i.e.~$100 = \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{100}\left|{x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right|}{100}$

$⇒ 10000 = 99\left|\lambda\right| + 97\left|\lambda\right| + 95\left|\lambda\right| + . . . . . + \left|\lambda\right|$

$+ \left|\lambda\right| + 3\left|\lambda\right| + 5\left|\lambda\right| + . . . . + 99\left|\lambda\right|$

$⇒ 2\left|\lambda\right| . \left(1 + 3 + 5 + . . . . + 99\right) = 10000$

$⇒ 2\left|\lambda\right| . \dfrac{50}{2} \times 100 = 10000$

$⇒ \left|\lambda\right| = 2$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm 2$

Now median of~$2\lambda, 4\lambda, 6\lambda, . . . . 200\lambda$~is~$\dfrac{100\lambda + 102\lambda}{2}$

$⇒ \text{Median} = 101\lambda = \pm 202$

questions.q:
If for some $x \in R$, the frequency distribution of the marks obtained by $20$ students in a test is:

Marks 2 3 5 7
Frequency distribution \left(x + 1\right)2$ \left(2x - 5\right)$ $x^{2} - 3x$ $x

Then the mean of the marks is :

$
questions.solution:
Total students $= 20$

$⇒ {\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} + \left(2x - 5\right) + \left(x^{2} - 3x\right) + x = 20$

$⇒ x^{2} + 2x + 1 + 2x - 5 + x^{2} - 3x + x = 20$

$⇒ 2x^{2} + 2x - 24 = 0 ⇒ x^{2} + x - 12 = 0$

$⇒ x = - 4, 3 \left(∵ x > 0\right)$

$∴ x = 3$

Average $= $\dfrac{{\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} \times 2 + \left(2x - 5\right)3 + 5\left(x^{2} - 3x\right) + 7 \times x}{20}

$= $\dfrac{32 + 3 + 0 + 21}{20} =$2.8$

Hence, required mean is~$2 . 8

$

questions.q: The variance of $50$ observations is $7$. If each observation is multiplied by $6$ and then $5$ is subtracted from it, then the variance of the new data is
questions.solution:
Let the observations be ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, {x}_{3}, \ldots , {x}_{50}$ and the mean be $\overset{¯}{x}$.

From the given data,

Variance~$= 7$, the number of observations \left(n\right) = 50$.

Variance~$= \dfrac{1}{n} ∑ \left({x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right)2$

$⇒ 7 = \dfrac{1}{50} ∑ \left({x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right)$2$

$⇒ 350 = ∑ \left({x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right)2 . . . \left(1\right)$~

Each observation is multiplied by $6$ and then $5$ is~subtracted.

Let the new observations be ${y}_{1}, {y}_{2}, {y}_{3}, \ldots , {y}_{50}$.

${y}_{i} = 6{x}_{i} - 5$

${x}_{i} = $\dfrac{{y}_{i} + 5}{6} . . . \left(2\right)$~

The new variance~$= $\dfrac{1}{n}$∑ \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2$

$\overset{¯}{y} = $\dfrac{1}{n}$∑ {y}_{i} . . . \left(3\right)$~

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = \dfrac{1}{50}∑ \left(6{x}_{i} - 5\right)$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = $\dfrac{1}{50}$∑ 6{x}_{i} - \mathop{∑}_{0}^{50}\dfrac{1}{50} $\cdot5$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = $\dfrac{1}{50}$∑ 6{x}_{i} - 5$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = 6\overset{¯}{x} - 5$~ ~[$∴$~From \left(1\right)$]

$⇒ \overset{¯}{x} = $\dfrac{\overset{¯}{y} + 5}{6} . . . \left(4\right)$~

$⇒ ∑ \left({x}_{i} - \overset{¯}{x}\right)2 = 350$

$⇒ ∑ \$left(\dfrac{{y}_{i} + 5}{6} - \dfrac{\overset{¯}{y} + 5}{6}\right)$2 = 350$~ [$∴$ From \left($2\right) \text{ and } \left(4\right)$]

$⇒ ∑ \left(\dfrac{1}{6}\rright)2 \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2 = 350$

$⇒ ∑ \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2 = 36 \times350$

$⇒ ∑ \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2 = 12600$

New variance$= \dfrac{1}{50}∑ \left({y}_{i} - \overset{¯}{y}\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{50} \times12600 = 252

questions.q: If $\overset{¯}{x}$~is the mean of $n$ observations ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, \ldots , {x}_{n}$~then the mean of the absolute deviations of these observations from $\overset{¯}{x}$& is
options: the mean proportion of the data
the standard deviation of the data
the mean deviation of the data
questions.solution:
If $\overset{¯}{x}$~is the mean of $n$ observations ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, \ldots , {x}_{n}$~then the mean of the absolute deviations of these observations from $\overset{¯}{x}$~is~the mean deviation of the data.

Here,

$\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + . . . + {x}_{n}}{n} . . . . \left(1\right)$

Mean deviation

$= \dfrac{\left|{x}_{1} - \overset{¯}{x}\right| + \left|{x}_{2} - \overset{¯}{x}\right| + . . . + \left|{x}_{n} - \overset{¯}{x}\right|}{n}$

$

questions.q: Assertion (A): The variance of the first $\mathrm{n}$ odd natural numbers is $\frac{n^2-1}{3}$. Reason (R): The sum of the first $\mathrm{n}$ odd natural numbers is $\mathrm{n}^2$ and the sum of the squares of the first $\mathrm{n}$ odd natural numbers is $\frac{n\left(4 n^2-1\right)}{3}$. Which of the following alternatives is correct?
options: (A) and (R) are true. (R) is correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct explanation of $(\mathrm{A})$
questions.solution: Sum of first $n$ odd natural numbers 1+3+5+\ldots . .+(2 n-1)=$\frac{n}{2}($1+2 n-1)=n² Sum of squares of first $n$ odd natural numbers $\begin{aligned}$& =$\sum($2 n-1)^2=$\sum\left($4 n²+1-4 n\right) \\ & =$\frac{4 n(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}-\frac{4 n(n+1)}{2}+$n \\ & =$\frac{2 n(n+1)(2 n+1)-6 n(n+1)+n}{3}$\\ & =$\frac{n}{3}\left($4 n²+6 n+2-6 n-6+3\right) \end{aligned} $\begin{aligned}$& =$\frac{n}{3}\left($4 n²-1\right) \\ & $\text { Variance }=\frac{\Sigma x_i^2}{n}-\left(\frac{\Sigma x_i}{n}\right)^2 \\  \text{ and }  =$\frac{n}{3 n}\left($4 n²-1\right)-\left(\frac{n^2}{n}\right)^2 \\ \text{ and } =$\frac{4 n^2-1}{3}-$n^2=$\frac{n^2-1}{3} \end{aligned}\therefore A$ and $R$ are true. $R$ is correct explanation of $A$.$

questions.q: Coefficient of variation of two distributions are $60%$ and $75%,$ and their standard deviation are $18$ and $15$ respectively, then their arithmetic means respectively are
questions.solution:
Given, $C{V}_{1} = 60, {CV}_{2} = 75, {\sigma}_{1} = 18$ and ${\sigma}_{2} = 15$
Let ${\overset{-}{x}}_{1}$ and ${\overset{-}{x}}_{2}$ be the means of ${1}^{st}$ and ${2}^{nd}$ distribution respectively.
Then, $C{V}_{1} = \dfrac{{\sigma}_{1}}{{\overset{-}{x}}_{1}} \times 100 ⇒ {\overset{-}{x}}_{1} = \dfrac{18 \times 100}{60} = 30$
$C{V}_{2} = \dfrac{{\sigma}_{2}}{{\overset{-}{x}}_{2}} \times 100 ⇒ {\overset{-}{x}}_{2} = \dfrac{15 \times 100}{75} = 20$
Hence, ${\overset{-}{x}}_{1} = 30$ and ${\overset{-}{x}}_{2} = 20$

questions.q: Let one observation equal to the mean is added to $n$ observations. If the variance changes from $78$ to $72$, then $n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Adding mean to the observations does not change the value of $∑ {\left({x}_{i} - \overset{-}{x}\right)}^{2}$, hence, 

$\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{\left({x}_{i} - \overset{-}{x}\right)}^{2}}{n}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n + 1}{\left({x}_{i} - \overset{-}{x}\right)}^{2}}{n + 1}\right)} = \dfrac{78}{72}$
$⇒ \dfrac{n + 1}{n} = \dfrac{78}{72} ⇒ n = 12$

questions.q:
The arithmetic mean of marks in Mathematics for four divisions A, B, C and D were 80, 75, 70 and 72 respectively. Their standard deviations were $12,6,8$ and and 10 respectively. Then, division
has more uniformity.
questions.solution:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \text { We know that C.V. }=\frac{\text { Standard Deviation }}{\text { Mean }} \\
& \therefore(\text { C.V. })_A=\frac{12}{18}=0.15 \text { and }(\text { C.V. })_B=\frac{6}{75}=0.08 \\
& (\text { C.V. })_C=\frac{8}{70}=0.11 \text { and }(\text { C.V. })_D=\frac{10}{72}=0.14
\end{aligned}
$$
C.V. is the least for division B.

questions.q:
Let $\overset{¯}{x}$,~$M$ and ${σ}^{2}$~be respectively the mean, mode and variance of $n$ observations ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, . ... , {x}_{n}$~and ${d}_{i} = - {x}_{i} - a, i = 1, 2, . ... , n,$~where $a$ is any number.

Statement I: Variance of ${d}_{1}, {d}_{2}, . . . , {d}_{n}$ is ${σ}^{2}$.

Statement II: Mean and mode of ${d}_{1}, {d}_{2}, . . . . , {d}_{n}$~are $- \overset{¯}{x} - a$~and $- M - a$, respectively.
options: Statement I and Statement II are both true&
Statement& I and Statement& II are both false&
Statement& I is true and Statement& II is false
Statement& I is false and Statement II is true
questions.solution:
Mean of ${d}_{1}, {d}_{2}, {d}_{3} . . . {d}_{n}$

$= ∑ \left(\dfrac{- {x}_{i} - a}{n}\right)

$= - \overset{→}{x} - a$

And, the mode of~${d}_{1}, {d}_{2}, {d}_{3} . . . {d}_{n}$ will be $- M - a$

Also, we know that~the variance~${\sigma}^{2}$ is unaffected by change of origin, hence it remains same.

$
